title: ioctl_finalize: state->inbuf_len always 0 at FINALIZE; AEAD decrypt outbuf undersized
description:
In ioctl_finalize() (crypto2dev_fd.c ~line 1394-1398):

    size_t need = CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN;
    if (state->inbuf_len > 0)
        need = max_t(size_t, need, state->inbuf_len + 16);
    ret = outbuf_grow(state, need);

state->inbuf is the pre-INIT write buffer (used by KEY_IMPORT / DO_KDF).
It is cleared by inbuf_clear(state) at line 782 when INIT is called.
By the time FINALIZE is called, state->inbuf_len is always 0 for a
properly-initialized OPERATION fd.

Consequence: the condition 'state->inbuf_len > 0' is always false at
FINALIZE time.  The outbuf is only grown by CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN (64 bytes).

For AEAD decrypt (wolfssl GCM batch path, kcapi AEAD): finalize() produces
up to inbuf_len bytes of plaintext (provider's internal inbuf, not state->inbuf).
wolfssl_aes_gcm_finalize() checks 'outbuf_size < inlen' and returns -EMSGSIZE.
kcapi_aead_finalize() checks 'outbuf_size < ctx->inbuf_len' and returns -EMSGSIZE.

This means AEAD decrypt finalize fails with -EMSGSIZE for any ciphertext
larger than what was already in the outbuf when FINALIZE is called.

The fix must reserve space for the provider's output size.  For AEAD decrypt,
the provider knows how much ciphertext it has buffered in ctx->inbuf_len,
but the framework does not have direct access to that.  Options:
  (a) Reserve CRYPTO2DEV_MAX_PAYLOAD for any AEAD algo (detectable by
      ops->set_aad != NULL or ops->set_tag != NULL).
  (b) Add a new ops callback (e.g. finalize_output_size()) for providers
      to report expected output size before finalize() is called.
  (c) Make the outbuf grow lazily inside outbuf_grow if needed.

The -EMSGSIZE return from finalize() is already caught (sets state->error = true),
so the failure is deterministic and not a silent data corruption.  However,
AEAD decrypt is completely broken for any message above ~CRYPTO2DEV_HASH_MAXLEN
bytes at finalize time.

Files: src/cdev/crypto2dev_fd.c (ioctl_finalize, ~line 1394)
